notes.meaning: Jerusalem faces a gathering enemy army and a harsh siege. The enemy treats Israel's leader with deep disrespect, even striking him on the face with a rod. This showed how low the royal house of David would be brought before God sent their promised deliverer.

Bethlehem was a small, humble village, yet God chose it to be the birthplace of the great Ruler over Israel. This promised King is the Messiah. His life did not start in Bethlehem, because He has existed with God from ancient times, from all eternity.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some historical scholars note that the concept of a pre-existing Messiah who existed before creation is not clearly found in early Jewish writings until the Similitudes of Enoch.

notes.meaning: God allows His people to endure trouble and exile for a time, much like a woman going through painful labor before a baby arrives. Deliverance comes when the child is born. After that, God will reunite His scattered people into one family.

differ.view: Some Reformed teachers understand the travailing woman as a picture of the nation of Israel suffering under trials until God restores them.
Many evangelicals read the travailing woman as Mary giving birth to Jesus, which brings an end to Israel's abandonment.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching identifies the woman giving birth as the Virgin Mary, linking this verse to the woman clothed with the sun in Revelation 12.

notes.meaning: The Messiah will care for His people with both the tenderness of a shepherd and the power of a mighty king. He leads them in the strength and majesty of the Lord. His flock will live in secure rest because His greatness will reach the ends of the earth.

The coming King will not only bring peace; He Himself will be peace for His people. When dangerous enemies invade and threaten to trample the land, God will raise up more than enough capable leaders to defend and protect His flock.
The rulers God raises up will overcome the lands of their oppressors and turn back their attacks. In this way, the Messiah rescues His people whenever hostile nations try to push past their borders.

God's surviving people will dwell among many nations as a refreshing blessing, like dew and gentle showers falling on the grass. Just as rain comes directly from heaven without waiting for human help, God gives this blessing purely by His own grace.

While God's people are a blessing to those who welcome them, they will also show fearless strength against those who attack them. Like a strong lion that cannot be stopped by other animals, God's people will overcome their foes through the Lord's power.
God promises complete victory to His people over all who oppose them. Because the Lord fights on their behalf, every enemy that rises up against them will finally be defeated.
The Lord announces that He will take away warhorses and chariots from His people. He does this in mercy so they will no longer depend on military weapons, but will put their whole trust in Him.
God will also pull down the fortified walls and military towers in their land. His people will live in safety without stone walls because the Lord Himself will be their fortress and protection.
The Lord will remove all witchcraft, magic charms, and fortune-tellers from the land. His people will turn away from secret occult arts and seek guidance only from the living God.
God will smash carved idols and sacred stone pillars so that false worship comes to an end. His people will no longer bow down in prayer to statues made by human hands.
The Lord will tear down the wooden poles used to worship the pagan goddess Asherah. He will also tear down the corrupt towns that housed and encouraged these sinful practices.
God will carry out justice in wrath against all nations that refuse to obey Him. This judgment reassures His people that evil will not win and that the Lord will put all things right.
